title: ABTS Radical Scavenging Capacity Measurement
author: Jing Xu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jirckd6
materials: Absorbance was measured at 734nm by Microplate Reader.

steps.title: Prepare extract stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried extracts in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to obtain a stock solution at a concentration of 10 mg mL⁻¹ for use in antioxidant assays.

steps.title: Generate ABTS⁺ radical solution
steps.instruction: Mix 10 mL of 7 mM ABTS solution with 10 mL of 2.45 mM potassium persulfate solution, let the mixture stand in the dark at room temperature for 12–16 h, then adjust the solution with ethanol until its absorbance at 734 nm is 0.70 ± 0.02 before use.

substeps.instruction: Combine 10 mL 7 mM ABTS and 10 mL 2.45 mM potassium persulfate.
Allow to stand in the dark at room temperature for 12–16 h.
Dilute with ethanol to reach A₇₃₄ = 0.70 ± 0.02.

steps.title: Dilute extracts in microplates
steps.instruction: Perform a two‑fold serial dilution of the 10 mg mL⁻¹ extract stock in a 96‑well microtitre plate according to the desired concentration series.

steps.title: Combine extracts with ABTS solution
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of each diluted extract (or 10 µL ethanol for the blank) to 195 µL of the prepared ABTS⁺ radical solution in the corresponding wells of the 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Incubate reaction mixtures
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 30 minutes in the dark.

steps.title: Measure absorbance and calculate RSA
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of each well at 734 nm, then calculate the percent radical scavenging activity using %RSA = [(A_blank – A_sample) / A_blank] × 100%; report the mean of triplicate measurements.
